newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity futures end mixed, COB higher.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity futures end mixed, COB higher.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures ended mixed Friday with California Oregon Border (COB) finishing higher on technical gains, industry sources said.
Although COB continued stronger on initial heating demand in the U.S. Northwest and some shortcovering, the contract needs to break $18.70 to continue an up trend of recent weeks, the sources said.

November COB finished 40 cents higher at $18.40 after trade in a range of $17.75-18.45, while December ended 25 cents higher at $19.40 after trade in a relatively narrow range to as low as $19.30 per megawatt hour (MWh), the sources said.
January COB settled 20 cents higher at $18.20 per MWh.
November Palo Verde (PV) finished down 16 cents at $17.24 after trade in a range of $16.85-17.65, while December finished down 10 cents at $17.65 per MWh after trade as high as $17.90.
NYMEX said a total of 164 COB and 103 PV contracts traded Friday.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
